AuthzAdminBindingView.description: One role binding: an account holds a role within a tenant.

account.description: The account the role is bound to.

granted_at.description: When the binding was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

role.description: The role bound to the account.

tenant.description: The tenant the binding belongs to.

AuthzAdminGrantView.description: One permission grant of a role: the permission it was written as, and the (resource, action) pair the policy engine matches on.

action.description: The action the grant matches on, kept beside the permission so an untranslatable grant can still be diagnosed.

created_at.description: When the grant was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

permission.description: The permission the (resource, action) pair translates to, for example authz.role.manage; the empty string when the pair matches no declared permission, which is a grant left from a vocabulary this process no longer carries.

resource.description: The resource the grant matches on, kept beside the permission so an untranslatable grant can still be diagnosed.

tenant.description: The tenant the grant belongs to.

dangerous.description: True when granting the permission widens the grantee's power over other accounts or over the tenant's policy; a client calls such a permission out before an operator grants it, and asks for a deliberate second confirmation.

description.description: The permission's description, rendered in the request's language from the key the declaring module gave it. Empty when the assembly delivers no message localizer or the module gave the permission no description key. A key no catalog carries comes back as the key itself, the i18n fallback; a client shows the text as received and does not resolve keys.

grantable.description: True when the caller holds the permission in the platform domain and may therefore grant it to a role. A permission the caller does not hold is still listed: the catalog is the whole declared set, not the caller's grantable subset.

group.description: The group the declaring module places the permission in, for example authorization or membership. Empty when the module gave it no group; a client groups such a permission as it sees fit.

permission.description: The permission name as the catalog declares it, for example authn.tenant.access. Only the authn.* permissions are the same vocabulary as authn.Action and carry its string; a permission outside it, such as authz.role.read, has no corresponding authn.Action.

AuthzAdminRoleView.description: One role of a tenant as the role routes report it.

builtin.description: True for a builtin role: the management face can neither rewrite nor remove it, nor change its grants. The mark is set by the host that seeds the policy data and is never cleared.

can_manage.description: True when the caller holds authz.role.manage in the platform domain, so a client renders the role, grant and binding controls. False hides them; the route guard still refuses a write the caller may not make.

created_at.description: When the role was written, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

description.description: The role's description as a client shows it: the operator's free text for a role this surface created, or a builtin role's description key rendered in the request's language. With no message localizer assembled, a builtin role answers its key itself, the i18n fallback.

member_count.description: How many active members hold the role. Null when the assembly delivers no account-identity reader: the count cannot be read, and the binding count is not a stand-in for it.

permission_count.description: How many permission grants the role holds, from one grouped read of the tenant's grants.

role.description: The role name within the tenant.

tenant.description: The tenant the role belongs to.

AuthzAdminRoleWrite.description: The body of a role write: the role's description. The builtin mark is not part of the body; a member sent under that name reaches nothing.

description.description: The role's free-text description, at most 500 characters. Absent leaves the stored text as it is; an explicit empty string clears it; an over-long value is a 400.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

delete.description: Removes the account's binding to the role within the tenant. An empty account is refused with a 400 before anything is written. A caller may not remove its own tenant-admin binding: that is refused with a 403 before anything is written, and another tenant administrator removes it. Removing a binding that does not exist succeeds with 204 and changes nothing. A mandatory audit row is written before the action; if it cannot be written the action is not carried out and the answer is 503.

delete.description: Revokes one permission from a role. The permission in the path is translated to its (resource, action) pair; a permission with no translation row is a 400. Revoking a grant the role does not hold succeeds with 204 and changes nothing, and a role that is not in the tenant is not refused: no grant row matches and the answer is also 204. A builtin role's grants cannot be revoked: that is a 409. A mandatory audit row is written before the action; if it cannot be written the action is not carried out and the answer is 503.

put.description: Grants one permission to a role. The permission in the path is checked against the catalog and translated to its (resource, action) pair before anything is written; a permission the catalog does not declare, or one with no translation row, is a 400 and no write happens. The role must exist in the tenant and must not be builtin: an absent role is a 400, and a builtin one is a 409, since its grants cannot be changed. Granting a permission the role already holds succeeds and leaves the existing row unchanged. A mandatory audit row is written before the action; if it cannot be written the action is not carried out and the answer is 503.
